summary: A neder is understood the way people talk. Someone who made a neder against "cooked food" may still eat roasted or boiled food.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against cooked food
chunks.st: In the case of one who vows that cooked foods

chunks.en: may eat roasted and boiled food.
chunks.st: are forbidden to him, he is permitted to eat roasted and boiled

chunks.en: If he said, "Konam, a cooked dish, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: foods, as they are not defined as cooked. If one said: Cooked food is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat soft food cooked in a pot,
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from tasting a loose cooked

chunks.en: but may eat thick food, and may eat a "trimita" egg
chunks.st: food but is permitted to taste a thick

words.note: An egg cooked in a special way.

chunks.en: and a gourd cooked in hot ashes.
chunks.st: one, which people do not generally refer to as a cooked food. And he is likewise permitted to eat a turemuta egg and the remutza gourd, as they are not considered cooked foods either.

summary: A neder against "food made in a pot" is different from a neder against "what goes down into a pot."

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against food made in a pot
chunks.st: In the case of one who vows that food cooked in a dish

chunks.en: is only forbidden in food boiled in it.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him, he is prohibited from deriving benefit only from food that is cooked by boiling

chunks.he: אָמַר, קוֹנָם הַיּוֹרֵד לַקְּדֵרָה שֶׁאֵינִי טוֹעֵם,
chunks.en: If he said, "Konam, what goes down into the pot, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: it in a dish. However, if one said: That which enters into a dish is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat anything cooked in a pot.
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from tasting anything cooked in a dish.

summary: A neder against "pickled," "boiled," "roasted," or "salted" food means the kind people usually call by that name. If he said "that I will not taste," it means all of that kind.

chunks.st: One who vows that pickled food
is forbidden to him is prohibited from
eating only pickled vegetables,

chunks.en: "Pickled food that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: as that is what people usually mean when referring to pickled food. However, if he says: Pickled food is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat any pickled foods.
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from tasting all pickled
foods. Similarly, one who vows that boiled food
is forbidden to him is prohibited from
eating only boiled meat,

chunks.en: "Boiled food that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: as that is the common meaning of the expression boiled food. On the other hand, if he says: Boiled food is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat any boiled foods.
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from eating all boiled foods.
One who vows that roasted food
is forbidden to him is prohibited from
eating only roasted meat;

chunks.en: these are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: "Roasted food that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: However, if one says: Roasted food is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat any roasted foods.
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from eating all roasted foods.
One who vows that salted food
is forbidden to him is prohibited from
eating only salted fish,

chunks.en: "Salted food that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: as that is the common meaning of the expression salted food. If, on the other hand, he says: Salted food is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: he may not eat any salted foods.
chunks.st: it, he is prohibited from eating all salted foods.

summary: A neder against "fish" includes every kind of fish, but not fish mixtures and fish sauce. The mishnah explains which fish foods are included in which nedarim.

chunks.en: "A fish," or "fishes, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: If one says: Fish or fishes are konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste
them,
he is prohibited from eating all of them, whether large fish or small,
whether salted or unsalted,
whether raw or cooked.

chunks.en: but he may eat chopped fish mix and fish sauce.
chunks.st: But he is permitted to taste minced sardines and to taste fish brine,

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against "tzachanah"
chunks.st: as these are not included in the common meaning of the word fish. One who vows that tzaḥana,

words.note: A dish of whole and chopped fish.

chunks.en: may not eat chopped fish mix,
chunks.st: a concoction of whole and chopped fish, is forbidden to him is prohibited from eating minced sardines

chunks.en: but may eat fish sauce and fish gravy.
chunks.st: as well, but he is permitted to eat fish brine and fish gravy [morays].

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against chopped fish mix
chunks.st: One who vows that minced sardines

chunks.en: may not eat fish sauce and fish gravy.
chunks.st: are forbidden to him is prohibited from eating fish brine and from eating fish gravy.

summary: The mishnah teaches if a neder against milk includes whey, the liquid left when cheese is made, and the other way around.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against milk
chunks.st: One who vows that milk
is forbidden to him is permitted to partake of whey [kum],
the liquid that separates from milk when it is made into cheese. But Rabbi Yosei prohibits
him from partaking of whey
. If one vows that whey is forbidden to him, he is permitted to partake of milk.
Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: someone who makes a neder against cheese
chunks.st: One who vows that cheese

chunks.he: אָסוּר בָּהּ בֵּין מְלוּחָה בֵּין טְפֵלָה:
chunks.en: may not eat it, whether salted or not salted.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him is prohibited from eating it whether it is salted or unsalted.

summary: A neder against meat does not include gravy, unless he said "this meat." Then anything that has its taste is forbidden.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against meat
chunks.st: One who vows that meat

chunks.en: may eat the gravy and the bits left in the pot.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him is permitted to eat gravy and sediments of boiled meat [kifa].

words.en: and with the bits left in the pot

chunks.st: But Rabbi Yehuda maintains that he is prohibited
from eating them. Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: There was a story, and Rabbi
chunks.st: There was an incident

chunks.en: Tarfon forbade us even eggs that were cooked with it.
chunks.st: where one took such a vow and Rabbi Tarfon prohibited us from even eggs that were cooked with meat.
The Rabbis said to him:
Indeed so,

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֹּאמַר בָּשָׂר זֶה עָלָי,
chunks.en: but when? When he says, 'This meat is forbidden to me.'
chunks.st: but when is this the halakha? When he says: This meat is forbidden to me,

chunks.en: Because if someone makes a neder against something and it gets mixed into something else,
chunks.st: referring to a specific piece of meat. This is because in the case of one who vows that an item is forbidden to him, and it becomes mixed into another

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ בְנוֹתֵן טַעַם, אָסוּר:
chunks.en: if it gives taste, it is forbidden."
chunks.st: item, if
chunks.stMore: the latter contains an amount of the forbidden food that gives it flavor, i.e., the forbidden food can be tasted in the permitted food, the mixture is forbidden. However, if one vows that meat in general is forbidden to him, without specifying a particular piece, only the meat itself is forbidden, not the gravy, sediments, or eggs cooked with that meat.

summary: A neder against wine or grapes, and what comes out of them. If he said "these grapes," then the wine from them is forbidden too.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against wine
chunks.st: Likewise, one who vows that wine

chunks.he: מֻתָּר בְּתַבְשִׁיל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם יַיִן.
chunks.en: may eat a cooked dish that tastes of wine.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him is permitted to eat a cooked dish that has the flavor of wine.

chunks.he: אָמַר קוֹנָם יַיִן זֶה שֶׁאֵינִי טוֹעֵם,
chunks.en: If he said, "Konam, this wine, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: However, if he said: Wine is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.en: and it fell into a cooked dish,
chunks.st: it, and the wine fell into a cooked dish,
if the dish contains an amount of the wine that gives it flavor,
it is forbidden.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against grapes
chunks.st: One who vows that grapes
are forbidden to him is permitted to partake of wine.
One who vows that olives
are forbidden to him is permitted to partake of oil.

chunks.en: If he said, "Konam, these olives and grapes
chunks.st: However, if one said: Olives and grapes are konam
for me, and for that reason I will not taste these

chunks.en: he may not eat them or what comes out of them.
chunks.st: items, he is prohibited from tasting them and the wine and oil that emerge from them.

summary: Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira and the Sages argue if a neder against a fruit also forbids the juice that is called by its name, like date honey.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against dates
chunks.st: One who vows that dates
are forbidden to him is permitted to eat date honey.

chunks.en: From late grapes, he may have vinegar made of late grapes.
chunks.st: One who vows that late grapes are forbidden to him is permitted to eat vinegar of late grapes.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

chunks.en: anything that what comes out of it is called by its name
chunks.st: In the case of any food that the name of its derivative is called after its

chunks.en: and he makes a neder against it,
chunks.st: name, i.e., the liquid that emerges from it bears its name, e.g., date honey or vinegar of late grapes, and one vows

chunks.en: he may not have even what comes out of it.
chunks.st: that the item itself, e.g., the grape, is forbidden to him, he is also prohibited from consuming the liquid that emerges from it.
But the Rabbis permit this.

summary: When a person says a plain word like "wine" or "oil," he means the usual kind. Other kinds that need an extra word, like "apple wine," are not included.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder against wine
chunks.st: One who vows that wine
is forbidden to him is permitted to partake of apple wine,
i.e., cider, as the unspecified term wine refers only to grape wine. One who vows that oil is
forbidden to him is permitted to partake of sesame oil,
as the unspecified term oil refers only to olive oil. One who vows that honey
is forbidden to him is permitted to eat date honey,
as the unspecified term honey refers only to bee honey. One who vows that vinegar

chunks.en: he may have vinegar of late grapes.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him is permitted to partake of vinegar of late grapes,
as vinegar is typically made from wine. One who vows that leeks
are forbidden to him is permitted to eat kaflutot,
a type of leek. One who vows that vegetables

chunks.en: he may eat wild vegetables of the field,
chunks.st: are forbidden to him is permitted to eat wild field vegetables,

chunks.en: because that is a name with an extra word.
chunks.st: as this type of vegetable has a modifier and is not referred to by the unspecified term vegetable.

summary: More examples of foods: which nedarim include which foods. Rabbi Yosi is often lenient.

chunks.st: One who vows that cabbage
is forbidden to him is prohibited from eating ispargus,
as that is a type of cabbage. However, one who vows that ispargus
is forbidden to him is permitted to eat cabbage.
One who vows that pounded beans

chunks.en: he may not eat bean stew,
chunks.st: are forbidden to him is prohibited from eating pounded bean stew [mikpa].
However, Rabbi Yosei rules that he is permitted
chunks.stMore: to eat it.One who vows that pounded beans are forbidden to him is prohibited from eating pounded bean stew. However, Rabbi Yosei rules that he is permitted to eat it.

chunks.st: One who vows that pounded bean stew
is forbidden to him is permitted to eat pounded beans
according to all opinions. One who vows that stew
is forbidden to him is prohibited from eating the garlic
of the stew. However, Rabbi Yosei rules that he is permitted
to eat the garlic
. One who vows that garlic is forbidden to him is permitted to eat stew.
One who vows that lentils

chunks.en: he may not eat lentil cakes,
chunks.st: are forbidden to him is prohibited from eating ashishim,
a dish made from lentils. However, Rabbi Yosei permits
it. It is agreed by all opinions that one who vows that ashishim
is forbidden to him is permitted to eat lentils.

chunks.en: "A wheat grain," or "wheat, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: If one says: Ḥitta, wheat in singular form, or ḥittim, wheat in plural form, are konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.he: אָסוּר בָּהֶן בֵּין קֶמַח בֵּין פָּת.
chunks.en: he may not eat them, whether flour or bread.
chunks.st: them, he is prohibited from eating wheat, whether as flour or bread.

chunks.en: "A crushed bean," or "crushed beans, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: If one says: Pounded bean or pounded beans are konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste

chunks.he: אָסוּר בָּהֶן בֵּין חַיִּין בֵּין מְבֻשָּׁלִים.
chunks.en: he may not eat them, whether raw or cooked.
chunks.st: them, he is prohibited from eating them, whether raw or cooked.
Rabbi Yehuda says

chunks.he: קוֹנָם גְּרִיס אוֹ חִטָּה שֶׁאֵינִי טוֹעֵם,
chunks.en: "Konam, a crushed bean or a wheat grain, that I will not taste,"
chunks.st: that if one says: Pounded bean or ḥitta is konam for me, and for that reason I will not taste
them, he is permitted to chew them raw, as that is not the normal way to eat them, and therefore was not included in the intention of the vow.
